$schema: Instance config for an ai-bridge control panel. Customize, then commit.
$people: EXAMPLE ONLY -- replace both entries below with your team's real GitHub login -> commit email pairs, HERE in this instance. The ai-bridge template is public, so it ships placeholder logins VERIFIED UNCLAIMED on github.com (example-user-007/008 both 404) and addresses at example.com, which RFC 2606 reserves and which cannot receive mail. If you write a new example, verify the login is unclaimed the same way: a plausible name like alice or bob is a real account, and an example naming a stranger is an example someone copies. The address is PER-INSTANCE, not per-person: the same login belongs to a different address in each group's bundle, because the address says which entity the work belongs to -- so never derive it from the login, and never move it into instance.config.local.json (that file says which login this clone IS). Used by scripts/commit-as.sh so each clone authors commits as the human running it; see SCHEMA.md 'Per-machine config overrides'. (install.sh offers to collect these when it stamps a NEW instance at a terminal; it never overwrites what is already here.)
$board: ON BY DEFAULT. true (or absent) => install.sh creates SNAPSHOT.json when missing, on any stamp, so this instance appears on the terminal board and its page can be rendered. false => never created, and the installer says so. NOTE: a snapshot is a LOCAL gitignored file — it does not publish anything. Publishing is a separate act (build-artifact-board.sh plus an Artifact URL), and question TEXT needs SNAPSHOT_QUESTION_TEXT=1 on top of that. So on-by-default is safe even for an instance that must not publish.
$advisor: OPTIONAL read-only tick observer. Add "advisor" to roles to enable it, and set roleTiers.advisor to pick its model (absent => light, the cheapest tier). Omit it and /pm-loop skips that step silently. Its concerns are adjudicated by the deep-tier project-manager before any human sees them, and it has no channel to worker agents, so a cheap model can never steer an expensive one.
